newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi reports Rangoon car attack to police - BBC.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi reports Rangoon car attack to police - BBC.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi said on Monday she had reported Saturday's attack on her motorcade by a stone-thowing crowd to the local police, the British Broadcasting Corporation's Burmese service reported.
"We opened a case at the Bahan Township police station," she said in a telephone interview to the BBC monitored here.

Asked if she knew anything about an investigation into the incident by the ruling Burmese military authorities, she said: "We don't know anything about it. Although it is said that an enquiry is being carried out, they haven't contacted us and asked us anything yet."

On Saturday, Suu Kyi's motorcade was attacked twice by a crowd pelting the vehicles with stones. Suu Kyi, who was unhurt in the attacks which smashed her car's windshield, later accused the government of orchestrating the incident.
A senior government official said on Monday the attacks were acts of sabotage from which the government had nothing to gain.

Diplomats said there was no doubt the government was involved to some extent in the incident. On Saturday there were about 2,000 young men in well-organised groups milling about near the Nobel peace laureate's house, outside barricades erected by the military government to prevent her from giving weekend speeches to supporters, they said.
They were from townships near Rangoon and were paid to come in and cause unrest, they added.
Britain and the United States have condemned the attack and demanded that the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) punish those responsible for the incident and protect Suu Kyi.

The Burmese government official denied state involvement in the incident and said somebody had committed an act of sabotage, although it was not necessarily Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party.
Suu Kyi also told the BBC that she was ready for dialogue with the SLORC as it was the only way to solve the current standoff between the government and the democracy movement.

"As we have said, it is through dialogue that all our problems must be solved. If they really love the country, they should walk on this road as soon as possible. We will always keep this road open," she said.
